title: Pre-event system check should validate the actual participant device/network requirements and block unsafe entry

original_titles.title: LB-02 system check covers only 4 items and never blocks entry

problem: The audit reports that the participant system check covers only a small number of items and does not block entry. Current route/component coverage needs a focused check against the actual event hardware/network policy.
impact: Participants may reach a timed level with an unsupported browser, viewport, upload capability or venue network, causing avoidable support incidents.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Define mandatory checks: supported browser/version, viewport, pointer/keyboard, secure context, storage availability, upload/download connectivity and clock synchronization.
Separate blocking checks from warnings and accessibility accommodations; do not block users solely for non-essential device characteristics.
Run checks before event entry and again before a timed level if critical capability has changed.
Provide a diagnostic summary that participants can copy to the help desk without exposing tokens or personal data.
Test with supported/unsupported browser profiles and network restrictions from the actual venue.

acceptance_criteria: Mandatory capability checks run before a timed level.
Failures are actionable and have an organizer override with audit trail.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
